scope: Remove executable NGE expertise modifiers from the active Publish 14.1 crafting, resource-sampling yield, structure-management, and retained cybernetic-crafting paths while preserving authored PRE-CU skill, resource, structure, and experimentation behavior. Close the complete OnCraftingExperiment callback inventory and distinguish the retained weapon-component coreLevel attribute from retired player combat-level authority.

findings: The pinned Publish 14.1 implementation has no expertise system or expertise-derived crafting modifiers.
The inherited active crafting path still allowed NGE expertise modifiers to raise resource-quality caps, alter experimentation rolls, and reduce crafted-item complexity.
Resource sampling yield and structure placement/load still allowed NGE expertise modifiers to increase yield, extraction rate, hopper size, and reduce power or maintenance costs.
The retained cybernetic crafting path allowed an NGE expertise modifier to reduce its authored protection penalty.
Persisted factory and harvester power-expertise objvars are removed when the compatibility helper runs so stale later-era state cannot remain authoritative.

The complete Java source tree contains exactly one OnCraftingExperiment callback. It dispatches into the authenticated PRE-CU resource, skill-mod, Force/city/food, and Luck experimentation path; its coreLevel argument is copied only into the authored weapon-component attribute of the same name and never reads or writes player combat level.
